title: Enterprise status and postmortem templates - customer-facing pack
body:
Purpose:
This is a living pack of customer-facing copy for enterprise incident communications: short status page updates (initial alert, ongoing updates, resolution) and concise postmortem summaries tailored for customer distribution. Use these as the canonical phrasing for CS reps and incident commanders when communicating externally.

Audience:
- Enterprise customers (SaaS buyers, platform teams)
- Customer Success and AE teams preparing outbound comms
- Legal/compliance for review where required

Notes to sender (quick rules):
- Keep status page updates short and time-stamped. No speculation.
- Use plain language; avoid deep technical jargon unless the customer requests it.
- Include expected ETA for next update if available.
- For regulated customers include a note: "If you require a formal compliance packet we will follow up via your security contact."
- Obtain ICS/Legal signoff for incidents with data exposure.

Template A: Initial status page / customer alert (short)
Subject: [Incident {{incident_id}}] Service disruption affecting Redwood API – investigating
Status page title: Partial outage affecting inference API in region {{region}}
Public status: Investigating
Message: We are currently investigating reports of increased error rates and failed requests for the Redwood inference API in {{region}}. Our engineering teams have identified a subset of requests experiencing timeouts and are actively working on remediation. Customers may notice elevated latencies or request failures for model inference during this period.
First observed: {{start_time}} UTC
Impact: Some requests to text generation and embedding endpoints may fail or return delayed responses. No indication of data exfiltration at this time.
Next update: We will provide an update within 30 minutes or sooner if the impact changes. For urgent questions, contact your CS rep or open a support ticket referencing {{incident_id}}.

Template B: Ongoing update (progress-focused)
Status page title: Incident {{incident_id}} — mitigation in progress
Public status: Degraded performance
Message: Engineering has identified a regression in the request routing layer that is causing uneven load distribution across serving pools. We have deployed a targeted routing rollback and are validating traffic patterns. Metrics show a 40% reduction in failed requests since the rollback started; we continue to monitor.
Customer impact: Continued intermittent timeouts for a subset of requests; most customers will see improved success rates as traffic stabilizes.
Actions taken: 1) Rolled back routing change at {{time_rollback}}; 2) Disabled burst autoscale temporarily; 3) Implemented a short-term traffic-shed for non-production tenants.
Estimated resolution: Monitoring; if metrics continue to improve we will move to resolved status and follow with a postmortem within 72 hours.
Next update: in 1 hour or upon resolution.

Template C: Resolution notification
Status page title: Incident {{incident_id}} — resolved
Public status: Resolved
Message: The incident impacting the Redwood inference API in {{region}} has been resolved as of {{resolution_time}} UTC. Root cause: a routing regression introduced in deployment {{deploy_id}} that caused disproportionate load on a subset of GPU pools. Mitigation: routing rollback and additional validation checks.
Customer impact: Affected requests should now succeed; if you continue to experience issues please contact support with {{incident_id}}.
Follow-up: A concise customer-facing postmortem will be published within 72 hours and shared with affected accounts.

Template D: Customer-facing postmortem summary (concise, non-technical)
Title: Post-incident summary — Incident {{incident_id}} ({{start_date}})
Overview: On {{start_date}} at {{start_time}} UTC we observed elevated error rates and latency for the Redwood inference API in {{region}}. This impacted customers using text generation and embedding endpoints. We resolved the issue at {{resolution_time}} UTC.
What happened (plain language): A recent change to our routing logic caused traffic to concentrate on a small number of serving instances, exceeding their capacity and resulting in timeouts for some requests.
Impact to customers: Intermittent failed requests and increased latency for a subset of users over approximately {{duration}}. No customer data leakage detected. Customers using dedicated capacity were less affected, but some experienced degraded throughput.
Root cause (brief): A routing configuration update in deployment {{deploy_id}} contained a condition that bypassed load-normalization for some traffic patterns. This went undetected in canary checks because the traffic distribution in canary did not match production mix.
Immediate mitigations: Rolled back the routing change, enforced traffic normalization flags, and increased pool capacity.
Preventative actions and timeline:
- Short term (0–72 hours): Replace the routing change with a guarded rollout gated by traffic distribution checks, longer canary windows.
- Mid term (2–4 weeks): Add synthetic traffic tests to our CI that mimic customer traffic mixes and validate routing normalization.
- Long term (1–3 months): Build automatic divergence alerts when pool utilization skew exceeds thresholds and introduce additional runbooks for automated safe-rollbacks.
Customer support offer: If you experienced lost productivity tied to the outage, please contact your AE/CS rep to log a formal impact report; we will prioritize restoration credits for verified business impact.
Questions and escalation: For follow-up, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or send email to enterprise-support@redwood.ai with subject "Postmortem {{incident_id}}".

Example filled postmortem (short):
- Incident ID: INC-2026-0423-1
- First observed: 2026-04-23 14:11 UTC
- Resolved: 2026-04-23 15:26 UTC
- Customer impact: ~7% of requests in eu-west-1 saw timeouts for ~75 minutes.
- Root cause summary: Routing change in deploy 2026-04-23-15 caused pool imbalance.
- Fix: rollback of deploy and temporary capacity increase.
- Next steps: synthetic traffic test added to CI; canary window extended to 2 hours.

CS checklist before sending to customers:
- [ ] Confirm incident ID and timestamps are accurate (engineering owner)
- [ ] Legal/Compliance review if data exposure or regulated customer impacted
- [ ] Product/Eng signoff on root cause language (no finger-pointing)
- [ ] AE/CS coordination: list of affected accounts and tailored messages for top-10 customers
- [ ] Link to detailed internal postmortem (for execs) and public postmortem page

Tone guide (short):
- Use clear, empathetic language.
- Own the problem. Avoid absolutes like "never"; prefer "we are taking steps to".
- Be specific about customer impact and next steps.

Edge cases and special phrasing for regulated customers:
- If incident touches customer data or PII: add line "We have no evidence at this time of unauthorized access to customer data. We will provide you a compliance packet with logs and retention details upon request."
- If incident affects single enterprise customer only, use a direct email with detailed timeline and an offer for a dedicated postmortem call.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide whether credits will be solely restorative (service credits) or include priority support hours for top-tier customers. (Action: CS leadership)
- Finalize wording for "no evidence of data exfiltration" with security team to avoid legal overreach.

Appendix: sample short messages for Slack/email to top customers
Slack DM subject: Incident {{incident_id}} — quick update
Message: Hi <customer-name> — we’re investigating increased errors for inference in {{region}}. We’ve rolled back a routing change and are seeing improvements. ETA for full resolution: ~30–60 minutes. Please DM me if you see anything critical.

Email subject: Update on recent service disruption (Incident {{incident_id}})
Email body: Hi <Name>,
We wanted to update you directly: earlier today we experienced a routing-related incident that affected inference in {{region}}. We have implemented a rollback and the service has recovered. We are compiling a short post-incident summary and will share it within 72 hours. If this impacted your production workflows we can schedule a call to review.

Document history (notes):
- 2026-04-08 A. Patel created initial draft.
- 2026-04-09 M. Liu: added regulated-customer phrasing and CS checklist.
- 2026-04-10 E. Chen: tightened postmortem language and added example incident.
